clue.text: Graceful birds close to shore, first to arrive in Welsh city

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter of the next word is kept
first points to the opening letter of the word that follows it, dropping the rest

blocks.note: swans are famously graceful birds
the last letter of shore
the first letter of arrive

explanation.surface: Elegant swans glide in near the beach as the first visitors to a Welsh coastal city.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a large port city on the south coast of Wales.

clue.text: Religious group or division

blocks.note: a sect is a religious group
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question of whether a body is a religious faction or a breakaway division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or' looks like it offers two definitions, but it simply supplies two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a distinct part or branch of something larger, such as an economy or city.

clue.text: A general out of the country

blocks.note: taken as written
general and broad both mean wide-ranging rather than specific

explanation.surface: An army general is away overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like a military officer; it is the adjective, as in broad terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Being abroad means being in a foreign land, away from your home nation.

clue.text: Resentful disparagement of us by Greek mimic on board

indicators.note: being on a ship means placed inside it, so the letters before go within the vessel's abbreviation

blocks.note: of us means belonging to us
Gr is the abbreviation for Greek
to ape is to mimic
on board conventionally means inside SS, the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Passengers on a ship are bitter because a Greek is imitating them.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from Aesop's fox, who called the grapes he could not reach sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sour grapes is the idiom for running down something because you cannot have it yourself.

clue.text: Greek writer a model brought over

indicators.note: brought over suggests being flipped over end to end, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
to model is to pose for an artist

explanation.surface: A Greek author has had a model shipped over to sit for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek storyteller credited with the famous collection of fables.

clue.text: Judge had robe torn

indicators.note: something torn is ripped apart, so the letters before it are pulled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A judge's gown has been ripped, an embarrassment in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a modern court judge in robes; the answer is the biblical figure from the Book of Judges.
explanation.definitionFit: Deborah was a prophetess who served as one of the leaders called judges of ancient Israel in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Outlaw peer, odd as can be

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters may become something else once rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A criminal nobleman is as strange as anyone could possibly be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd as can be' reads as one phrase meaning very strange; 'odd' is in fact part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless bandit or criminal of the Wild West kind, an outlaw.

clue.text: Gathering, following complaint

blocks.note: a bee is a social gathering, as in a sewing bee
f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A meeting called after someone lodged a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: A bee in the sense of a gathering is chiefly American: a spelling bee or quilting bee.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is informal slang for a grievance or grumble, as in having a beef with someone.

clue.text: Oilfield firefighter delivered a challenge, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

blocks.note: to deliver a speech is to read it out, and a challenge is a dare

explanation.surface: Someone issued a challenge out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Adair was a famous American who put out oil well fires, including in Kuwait in 1991. 'Read' in the past tense sounds like red.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul 'Red' Adair made his name battling blazing oil wells around the world.

clue.text: Why 12 unfolded involving a secluded spot

indicators.note: unfolded means opened out into a different shape, so the letters are rearranged
involving means wrapping around something, so the single letter goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
the answer to 12 across
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wondering why a thought came out about a secret retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideaway is a secluded or concealed retreat where one can escape notice.

clue.text: Caught four at sea making for an Ionian island

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters of the number are muddled

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: Four sailors or fish are caught while heading across the sea towards a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is one of the Greek islands in the Ionian Sea, off the north-west coast of Greece.

clue.text: Stayed over on South American peninsula,

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the word for finished is sent to the end behind the place letters

blocks.note: S is the compass abbreviation for South
US stands for the United States, hence American
P is a map abbreviation for peninsula
something that is over has finished

explanation.surface: Someone stopped off for a stay on a peninsula in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as published ends in a comma, so it may have lost a few words. 'On' places the finished word after the geographical letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stayed execution is a suspended one: both mean halted or postponed for a time by order.

clue.text: Rind found in a green Opel, rotted

indicators.note: something rotted has decayed and fallen apart, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written; Opel is a German car maker

explanation.surface: Some fruit skin has been left to rot in an old green Opel car.
explanation.definitionFit: Rind is the tough outer skin of a citrus fruit, and this is the skin of the commonest such fruit.

clue.text: Almost perfect concept

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the next word is dropped

blocks.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: A notion that is nearly flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: A concept is a notion or thought formed in the mind, a direct synonym.

clue.text: We lingered, upsetting comedic US actor

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over and disordering, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Our lingering annoyed a funny American film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Gene Wilder was the American comic actor of Willy Wonka and Young Frankenstein fame.

clue.text: The Parisienne girl (married girl) in a Spanish-speaking area

blocks.note: la is the feminine form of 'the' in French, as a Paris woman would say
a girl's name
M is the standard abbreviation for married
another girl's name

explanation.surface: A French woman's daughter, now married, has settled somewhere Spanish is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: The countries of Central and South America are mostly Spanish-speaking, a whole region of the world.

clue.text: Thoroughly fashionable 24 elsewhere

blocks.note: in means fashionable
the answer to 24 down is a team, and a side is a team
someone out is not here but somewhere else

explanation.surface: A stylish team playing away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 down's answer must itself be swapped for a synonym before use.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something inside out is to know it completely, so the phrase means thoroughly.

clue.text: Mrs Mopp is making personal appeal

blocks.note: Mrs Mopp was the charwoman in the old BBC radio comedy ITMA, and a char is a cleaner
taken as written
the opening two letters of making

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady is drawing people to her through charm.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is British for a cleaning woman. The last two letters come from the start of 'making', without an explicit signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling attractiveness or charm that inspires devotion in others.

clue.text: Veteran soldier in TA slowed alarmingly

indicators.note: alarmingly suggests something has gone badly awry, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ageing soldier in the reserves has become worryingly slow.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Old sweat is British slang for an experienced soldier who has served for many years.

clue.text: I pay a flying visit on a regular basis

definitions.text: I pay a flying visit on a regular basis

blocks.clueFragment: I pay a flying visit on a regular basis
blocks.note: surface reading: a busy person who regularly pops in briefly

blocks.clueFragment: flying visit on a regular basis
blocks.note: setter's reading: a celestial body that literally flies past Earth roughly every 76 years

explanation.walkthrough: A flying visit is a short call, but here the visitor really flies, returning on a fixed cycle through the solar system.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous periodic comet named after Edmond Halley returns to the inner solar system about every 76 years.

clue.text: More would have us believe this is the perfect place

definitions.text: More would have us believe this is the perfect place

blocks.note: surface reading: someone claims a place is even better than it seems
setter's reading: Sir Thomas More, author of a 1516 book describing an ideal island society

explanation.walkthrough: The capital M on 'More' is hidden by its place at the start of the sentence; it is the Tudor statesman, not a comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More coined the name for his imagined ideal commonwealth, now a general word for any perfect society.

clue.text: A Mediterranean islander in strange trance

indicators.note: strange means unusual or out of the ordinary, so the letters are made into an odd new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A person from a sunny island is in a peculiar dreamlike state.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cretan is a native of Crete, the largest Greek island in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Spots river by wood

blocks.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: Someone notices a river beside some woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' reads as a verb meaning notices, but it is the noun: red marks on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash is an outbreak of red spots or blotches on the skin.

clue.text: Notice clergyman’s in control

blocks.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
a minister is a clergyman; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A notice announces that the vicar is now in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer something is to manage or run it, which is to have control of it.

clue.text: Blundering writer shown up in it

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards
in places the writing tool inside the final word

blocks.note: a pen is something you write with
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clumsy author is exposed and embarrassed.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or incompetent, lacking the skill to do something properly.

clue.text: Group of players from Reigate, amateurs

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow, running across them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the town and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A sports side made up of amateurs from the Surrey town of Reigate.
explanation.definitionFit: A team is a group of players who compete together in a game.

clue.text: Docker set off, drove recklessly, ending in catastrophe

indicators.note: set off is read as letters set in motion and scattered out of order
driving recklessly throws things about, so these letters too are jumbled
the ending of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the last letter of catastrophe

explanation.surface: A dock worker set off and drove dangerously, ending in a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore is a labourer who loads and unloads ships in a port, the same job as a docker.

clue.text: Drank around base

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: to tope is an old word meaning to drink alcohol heavily

explanation.surface: Someone had a drink somewhere on a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: Tope is a dated word for drinking to excess, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a military establishment or storage base where supplies and troops are kept.

clue.text: Reserves come back to draw, making a try

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way you came, so these letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
to draw someone in is to tempt or entice them

explanation.surface: Reserve players return to the field to level the score with a try in rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby picture makes 'try' look like a score, and 'draw' a tied result; both are read in other senses.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is an effort to do something, which is what a try is outside rugby.

clue.text: Land turtle losing power

indicators.note: losing something means it goes missing, so the named letter is taken out

blocks.note: a terrapin is a small freshwater turtle
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A tortoise or turtle on land runs out of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land considered for its physical features, such as rough or hilly ground.
